scope: Bounded local model two-pass single-card review; not independent human approval.

cards.title: Chain of Command
cards.instruction: Treat every question, favor, and decision as something that must travel through the proper hierarchy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your request for a teaspoon must go through the kitchen supervisor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then countersign your request. I'll pass it up to catering.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 routes a teaspoon request through the supervisor; A5 requires countersigning and onward transmission to catering.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 distinguishes B2's physical access from authority; A5 uses B4's supervisor identity to change the required procedural step.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants a readily available teaspoon and B4 supplies the exact rank A1 required.

heightening.evidence: A5 responds to B4 satisfying the first requirement by requiring a further hierarchical stage.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a teaspoon request and B2 puts A beside the teaspoons, making the obstruction immediately playable.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's distinction between proximity and authority neatly expresses why A refuses an easy favor.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 routes a teaspoon request through supervision; A3 rejects proximity as authority; A5 requires countersigning and upward routing.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's proximity argument causes A3's authority distinction; B4's rank revelation causes A5's revised authorization procedure.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants immediate access to nearby teaspoons and B4 supplies the rank A requested, forcing a new procedural response.

heightening.evidence: B4 satisfies the first authority requirement, but A5 adds countersigning and a higher catering level.

specificity.evidence: A1 and B2 establish a tiny kitchen favor and accessible teaspoons; the opening is intentionally bureaucratic rather than conversationally relaxed.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'Physical proximity is not authority' crisply defines the obstruction, and A5 earns its new layer from B4's rank.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 argues physical access makes compliance easy; A3 explicitly distinguishes access from authority.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 identifies B as supervisor; A5 assigns that rank countersigning duties before further routing.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A treats even a teaspoon favor as dependent on hierarchical authorization.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: Meeting the named authority condition reveals a further approval layer.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A makes a trivial favor travel through successive authorized levels even when the requested object is immediately accessible.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Generic bureaucracy: A1 and A5 specify ranks and upward routing, rather than paperwork required for its own sake.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: B4's declaration of rank changes A5's treatment of B from requester needing a supervisor to supervisor needing a higher routing stage.

records.recommendedEdit: Retained unchanged at 92 after re-reading. B4 materially changes A5's procedural requirement while preserving the teaspoon request. Five spoken ABABA turns, under 75 words; hard gates pass.
records.remainingConcern: Catering's higher position is newly asserted in A5, though coherent with the kitchen setting. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: Catering's higher authority is introduced only in A5, though it is coherent within the illustrative workplace.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative a applies institutional hierarchy to a workplace favor; b invents domestic departments and handles temporary authority.
